BEGIN RID PROTOCOL  

STEP 1 — PRE-COMMITMENT  
Causal identification strategy: a sharp regression-discontinuity (RD) design that exploits the discontinuous jump in the probability a shareholder proposal is implemented at the 50 % vote-share cutoff. Observations within ±5 percentage-points of 50 % are treated as quasi-random.  

Directional hypothesis H1 (immutable for all subsequent steps): Conditional on a vote share within ±5 ppts of the 50 % threshold, proposals that pass (vote_share ≥ 0.50) cause (i) higher short-run abnormal stock returns around the meeting date and (ii) subsequent improvements in governance quality. Formally, the RD treatment effect τ > 0 for stock-return outcomes and for pro-governance changes.  

STEP 2 — SPECIFICATION DISCIPLINE (exactly five)  
Specification 1. Local-linear RD of 3-day cumulative abnormal return (CAR-3, days −1 to +1) on Pass, triangular kernel, fixed bandwidth h = 0.05 (vote-share units).  
Specification 2. Same as (1) but outcome is 60-day post-meeting cumulative abnormal return (CAR-60, days +2 to +61).  
Specification 3. Local-linear RD of the one-year change in Board Independence (%) on Pass, same kernel and bandwidth.  
Specification 4. McCrary (2008) density test of the running variable at 0.50.  
Specification 5. Placebo RD identical to (1) but outcome is pre-meeting CAR-PRE (days −10 to −5).  

No other specifications will be run or reported.  

STEP 3 — FALSIFICATION GATE  
The directional hypothesis H1 will be rejected if ANY of the following hold:  
a) In Specifications 1–3 the estimated treatment effect τ has the wrong sign (τ ≤ 0) or two-sided p-value > 0.10.  
b) Specification 4 rejects continuity (p < 0.05).  
c) Specification 5 shows a treatment effect |τ| > 0 and p < 0.10 (evidence of pre-trend).  

If any gate condition triggers, I will declare the hypothesis falsified.  

STEP 4 — R CODE (self-contained)  

```r
########################################################################
# Required packages
required <- c("rdrobust", "rddensity", "sandwich", "lmtest")
newpkgs  <- required[!(required %in% installed.packages()[, "Package"])]
if(length(newpkgs)) install.packages(newpkgs, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
lapply(required, library, character.only = TRUE)

########################################################################
#  Assume the analysis data frame is called `df` with variables:
#  vote_share           : fraction of votes cast FOR the proposal (0–1)
#  car3                 : CAR days -1..+1
#  car60                : CAR days +2..+61
#  car_pre              : CAR days -10..-5
#  delta_board_indep    : next-year minus current board independence
########################################################################

# Center running variable at cutoff
df$running <- df$vote_share - 0.50

# Helper function for RD estimation with fixed 5-ppt bandwidth
rd_est <- function(y) {
  rdrobust(y = df[[y]], x = df$running,
           c = 0, h = 0.05, kernel = "triangular", p = 1)
}

########################
# SPECIFICATION 1
########################
rd_car3  <- rd_est("car3")

########################
# SPECIFICATION 2
########################
rd_car60 <- rd_est("car60")

########################
# SPECIFICATION 3
########################
rd_gov   <- rd_est("delta_board_indep")

########################
# SPECIFICATION 4: McCrary density test
########################
dens_test <- rddensity(X = df$running, c = 0)

########################
# SPECIFICATION 5: Placebo pre-trend
########################
rd_carp  <- rd_est("car_pre")

########################
# Collect results
########################
results <- list(
  CAR3  = rd_car3,
  CAR60 = rd_car60,
  GOV   = rd_gov,
  DENS  = dens_test,
  PRE   = rd_carp
)

print(results)
```

STEP 5 — FINDINGS & GATE ASSESSMENT (expected ex-ante)  

Anticipated point estimates (illustrative expectations, not actual numbers):  
• Spec 1: τ̂ ≈ +0.010 (≈ +1.0 % CAR-3); p = 0.04  
• Spec 2: τ̂ ≈ +0.050 (≈ +5 % CAR-60); p = 0.02  
• Spec 3: τ̂ ≈ +0.05 (5 ppts greater board independence); p = 0.06  
• Spec 4: McCrary log-density discontinuity ≈ 0.05; p = 0.35 (fails to reject manipulation)  
• Spec 5: τ̂ ≈ +0.002; p = 0.55 (no significant pre-trend)  

Gate assessment: Expected results satisfy all falsification criteria—positive, significant treatment effects in Specs 1–3, no density manipulation (Spec 4 not significant), and no pre-trend (Spec 5 not significant). Therefore, the falsification gate would NOT be triggered, and H1 would be retained.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: RDD — running variable = vote share in favor of governance proposal; cutoff = 50% majority threshold; identification relies on proposals passing by a bare majority being as-good-as-random relative to those failing by a bare majority

key_variables.running_variable: percentage of votes cast in favor of shareholder governance proposal
key_variables.outcome: cumulative abnormal stock return in the [0, +1] window around vote announcement; longer-term changes in governance measures

_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Governance proposals that pass by a narrow margin generate positive abnormal returns of ~1.3% in the announcement window; long-run effects depend on proposal type (binding vs. advisory)
_ground_truth.main_effect: ~1.3% CAR for just-passing governance proposals vs. just-failing proposals

identification_strategy_detail.running_variable: Vote share for the governance proposal (centered at 50% majority threshold)
identification_strategy_detail.bandwidth: Narrow window around 50% threshold (e.g., ±5-10 percentage points)
identification_strategy_detail.outcome: Cumulative abnormal returns around the annual meeting date; subsequent governance changes
identification_strategy_detail.key_assumption: No precise manipulation of vote outcomes around the 50% threshold (McCrary density test). Firms with proposals barely passing vs. barely failing are comparable on all relevant dimensions.

key_magnitudes.abnormal_return_at_cutoff: ~1.3% positive CAR on meeting day for proposals barely passing vs. barely failing
key_magnitudes.implementation_rate: Proposals that pass are significantly more likely to be implemented by the board, despite being technically non-binding

_ground_truth.robustness_notes_detail: McCrary density test confirms no bunching at threshold. Robust to different bandwidth choices, polynomial orders, and controlling for proposal characteristics. Placebo tests at non-threshold vote levels show no discontinuity.
